solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: One third of fruit’s been eaten? Get stuck in (6)

indicators.note: what has been eaten is no longer there, so that third of the fruit disappears

blocks.note: a greengage is a green plum
the first three of its nine letters, the part eaten

annotation.surface: Someone finds a bitten piece of fruit and urges a companion to tuck in.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'been eaten' is the instruction, not part of a picnic: a third of the plum is bitten off the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to get stuck in, British slang for throwing yourself into a task or fight, is to join battle.

entries.clue: I think I’m in the wrong dance (6-2)

definitions.text: I think I’m in the wrong

blocks.clueFragment: I think I’m in the wrong
blocks.note: the polite phrase that opens a correction or apology
an old ballroom dance where anyone may tap a shoulder and cut in

annotation.surface: A flustered dancer realises they have wandered into the wrong dance.
annotation.walkthrough: An excuse-me is an old-fashioned ballroom dance in which you may tap a dancer's shoulder and claim their partner; the phrase is also how you politely admit a slip.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the phrase said when owning up to a blunder, and the ballroom dance named after the words used to cut in.

entries.clue: Roman emperor good with Scotland (5)

blocks.note: G = good
Alba is the Gaelic name for Scotland

annotation.surface: A Roman emperor teams up with Scotland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: he ruled briefly after Nero, in the year of four emperors, AD 69.

entries.clue: Partly engineering a machine to remove cotton seeds (3)

definitions.text: a machine to remove cotton seeds

indicators.note: only part of the next word is used, so look inside it

blocks.note: letters three to five of this word

annotation.surface: A description of a cotton gin as a piece of engineering.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer sits in the only word that looks like part of the definition, which is why the hiding place is easy to overlook.
annotation.definitionFit: A dictionary definition: Eli Whitney's 1793 cotton engine, shortened to gin, pulls fibre away from seed.

entries.clue: Second key Oscar and BAFTA, say, for original direction of Titanic (8)

blocks.note: S = second
E is a musical key
both are film prizes; 'say' marks them as examples

annotation.surface: Film-prize talk about the movie Titanic, which won eleven Oscars.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about the film; the definition is about the ship. 'Oscar' is not O here: the whole phrase is one piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: the liner set out from Southampton heading toward open ocean, and never made port.

entries.clue: Queen one earl upset (7)

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, its letters tumbling into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A queen has upset one of her earls.
annotation.walkthrough: Eleanor of Aquitaine and Eleanor of Castile were both English queens.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a royal name borne by several medieval English consorts.

entries.clue: Crop weight reduced during unseasonable warmth (6,5)

indicators.note: a word reduced is cut down to its standard abbreviation
one thing happening during another sits within it, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: warmth at the cold time of year is out of season
W is the abbreviation for weight

annotation.surface: A farmer worries that a warm spell out of season has cut the weight of the harvest.
annotation.walkthrough: The farming surface makes 'reduced' look like a smaller yield; it only shortens a word to one letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a cereal sown in autumn to overwinter and be harvested the next summer.

entries.clue: Be frightened under cars being repaired (3,6)

indicators.note: something being repaired is taken apart and put back together, here in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A mechanic is nervous about lying under cars while they are being fixed.
annotation.walkthrough: The garage picture makes 'under' look like a position, but it is just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to behave in a panicky way, as if fleeing from a threat.

entries.clue: Saw Twitter introducing a letter signifying unknown (6)

indicators.note: to introduce is to bring in, so the second part goes into the first

blocks.note: birds twitter, that is sing
A, plus Y, a letter used in algebra for an unknown

annotation.surface: A social-media post that brings in the letter used for an unknown, as in X or Y.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twitter' with its capital T looks like the social network, but here it is birdsong. 'Saw' is the noun, not the past of see.
annotation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned sense: a saw is a proverb, a wise old maxim.

entries.clue: Director and unsubtle actor get ready in the UAE (6)

blocks.note: DIRECTOR cut short to its first three letters
a ham is an actor who overplays

annotation.surface: A film director and an over-the-top actor prepare to shoot in the Emirates.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not prepared but a noun: ready money, cash.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword sense of ready, meaning cash, pinned to a place: the currency of the United Arab Emirates.

entries.clue: A sign of spring — family eat outside house at last (9)

indicators.note: the family and the eating stay outside, wrapping around the next piece
at last means at the very end, so take only the final letter

blocks.note: a clan is a family group
dine = eat
last letter of housE

annotation.surface: An early-spring family meal eaten outdoors, outside the house.
annotation.walkthrough: The first two pieces run together and wrap round the single letter, which lands just after the opening C.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the lesser celandine is a little yellow flower among the first to bloom each year.

entries.clue: Be very protective of girl in US city (5)

indicators.note: the girl is in the city, so her letters sit inside its abbreviation

blocks.note: NY = New York
a girl's name

annotation.surface: A parent is anxious about a daughter living in an American city.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb, to fuss over someone.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb from the noun: to treat someone as a children's nurse would, coddling them.

entries.clue: Bread or dough? No big difference (5,6)

blocks.note: bread and dough are both slang for money, here the loose coins kind
a minor alteration, read literally

annotation.surface: A baker shrugs that bread and dough are much the same thing.
annotation.walkthrough: The baking picture hides that bread and dough are both slang for money.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: coins in the pocket, money in slang; and, read word by word, an alteration that is only slight.

entries.clue: Queen not wanting to be spotted on stage? (4,7)

definitions.text: Queen not wanting to be spotted on stage?

blocks.note: a royal who wishes to avoid something
surface: seen in the theatre; meant: a queen in a play whose hand is marked with a spot of blood she cannot wash off

annotation.surface: A royal who hopes no one will notice her on the stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' seems to mean seen; it means marked with a spot, the bloodstain she tries to scrub from her hands in Shakespeare's play.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue: Shakespeare's Scottish queen is desperate to be rid of the spot of blood on her hand.

entries.clue: Have the ability to finish off academic article (3)

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its end, so take the letter it finishes with

blocks.note: last letter of academiC
an is the indefinite article

annotation.surface: A scholar able to complete a paper for a journal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like the paper being finished, but it is the grammatical kind.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the modal verb of being able.

entries.clue: A check on waterproof road surface (7)

indicators.note: in an across clue, 'A check on waterproof' puts the check after, on the end of, the raincoat

blocks.note: a mac is a raincoat
as printed
a dam checks a river's flow

annotation.surface: An inspection to confirm a road's surface keeps water out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Waterproof' reads as an adjective for the road; it is the noun, a raincoat.
annotation.definitionFit: A dictionary sense: the compacted broken-stone paving named after John McAdam.

entries.clue: Country long showing significant growth (5,4)

blocks.note: the South American country
to pine for is to long for

annotation.surface: A country showing strong economic growth over a long period.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Growth' sounds economic; it is a plant. 'Long' is a verb, to yearn.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: the monkey puzzle tree, a large conifer, is literally something grown, and a big one.

entries.clue: Deserts, concerned with local political division (6)

definitions.note: Deserts is plural as in 'just deserts'; REWARD is singular

blocks.note: re = concerning
a ward is an electoral district of a town

annotation.surface: Someone abandons a cause out of worry over local ward politics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deserts' looks like a verb, abandons; it is the noun in 'just deserts', stressed like the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: your deserts are what you have earned, good or bad, so the positive side fits.

entries.clue: Twerk for dancing? This must be cut out (8)

indicators.note: dancing letters jig about and land in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Someone disapproves of twerking and wants it banned from the dance floor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut out' sounds like stop it; here it is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: ornamental patterns sawn out of thin wood with a fine saw are, by nature, cut out.

entries.clue: Column briefly mentions iconic characters primarily associated with the cinema (6)

indicators.note: said briefly, the word is cut short by its last letter
primarily means first of all, so take the first letters

blocks.note: FILE (a column of people) without its last letter
first letters of Mentions Iconic Characters

annotation.surface: A newspaper column name-drops iconic film characters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Column' is not newspaper writing but a file, a line of people one behind another.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the adjective for things of or like the movies.

entries.clue: Preserved vessel lost power (7)

blocks.note: a can is a container
an engine or battery dies

annotation.surface: A historic ship kept as a museum piece that has lost its engine power.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Preserved' calls up a museum ship; it is fruit kept in sugar.
annotation.definitionFit: A narrower sense: fruit or peel kept by steeping in sugar syrup.

entries.clue: Character Ibsen created in Councillor, a big cheese? (7)

indicators.note: the character is created in the councillor, so her name goes inside

blocks.note: CR is the abbreviation for councillor
Hedda Gabler, heroine of Ibsen's play

annotation.surface: A theatre figure asks whether a local councillor is really an important person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Big cheese' means a bigwig, but here it is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, with a wink: the Somerset hard cheese is traditionally made in large wheels.

entries.clue: Compel using spoken Gaelic when having company over (6)

indicators.note: a spoken word is heard, not seen, so take its sound and spell it another way
in a down entry, something over sits above, so the company comes first

blocks.note: CO = company
Erse is an old name for Gaelic

annotation.surface: Forcing guests to speak Gaelic when they come round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Having company over' paints a dinner party; it just places one piece on top of the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to force someone to act by pressure or threat.

entries.clue: Friend had sense of taste (6)

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
had a meal = ate

annotation.surface: A friend with good taste.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Had' seems to be possession; it is eating, as in 'had lunch'.
annotation.definitionFit: A transferred sense: the roof of the mouth, once thought the seat of taste, came to mean the faculty itself.

entries.clue: One step saving leader (3)

indicators.note: 'saving' can mean except, as in 'saving your presence', so the leader is left out

blocks.note: a pace is a step
the first letter, removed

annotation.surface: A single step that rescues a leader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saving' reads as rescuing but means except.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the card or die face with a single pip counts as one.

entries.clue: State current saving after what HS2 no longer will do to Leeds? (11)

blocks.clueFragment: what HS2 no longer will do to Leeds
blocks.note: the HS2 high-speed rail line's eastern leg to Leeds was scrapped
I is the symbol for electric current
a saving is a cut in spending

annotation.surface: A complaint about the British government's cost-cutting on the HS2 rail line.
annotation.walkthrough: HS2 is a British high-speed railway whose Leeds leg was cancelled to save money. The clue lists pieces out of order: 'after' puts the railway phrase first.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the six New England states of the US.

entries.clue: Terrier — mine’s escaped from Pacific island (5)

indicators.note: what has escaped from somewhere is no longer in it, so the mine leaves the island

blocks.note: home of the Bounty mutineers' descendants
a pit is a mine, removed

annotation.surface: A dog that has run away from a mine on a Pacific island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mine's' reads as possessive, my dog; it is 'mine has', a coal pit.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a small, shaggy Scottish breed of terrier.

entries.clue: Almost every diver wanting protection for breathing (5)

indicators.note: almost all of a word is the word just short of complete, so drop its last letter
a word lacking protection has lost its outer letters, the shell around its middle

blocks.note: ALL (every) without its last letter
DIVER without its outer letters D and R

annotation.surface: Nearly every diver lacks breathing apparatus.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Protection' looks like diving gear; it is the outside of the word itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anything still drawing breath is living.

entries.clue: Unknown coin got in change (9)

indicators.note: as a verb, to change the letters is to swap them round

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A strange coin turned up among someone's loose change.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like coins, matching 'coin', but it tells you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: travelling under a false identity, so not recognised.

entries.clue: Idol in precious metal, not large (3)

indicators.note: 'not large' means without the L, so that letter comes out

blocks.note: gold is a precious metal
L = large, removed

annotation.surface: A statue of a false god cast in precious metal, but not a big one.
annotation.walkthrough: The golden calf is the idol the surface calls up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an object of worship, a deity or its image.

entries.clue: What cuts light from space views? Pluto mainly (8)

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so all but the last letter

blocks.note: to eye is to view, so eyes = views
Hades, the Greek counterpart of Pluto, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Astronomy talk: what blocks the light from space in pictures of Pluto?
annotation.walkthrough: Pluto is the god of the underworld, not the dwarf planet; the Greeks called him Hades. 'Space' is only the room in front of your face.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a visor worn on the brow that blocks glare from the open air around you.

entries.clue: Shifting sand blocks Greek port (6)

indicators.note: shifting sand moves about, its letters landing in a new order
the sand blocks the abbreviation by sitting in its middle

blocks.note: GK = Greek
the four letters rearranged

annotation.surface: Drifting sand is silting up a harbour in Greece.
annotation.walkthrough: The Greek setting is a decoy: the port is Polish, on the Baltic.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a major Baltic seaport in northern Poland.
